title: A Methodological Framework for Explicit Control of the Speed-Accuracy Trade-off in Brain-Computer Interfaces
summary: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are limited by low signal-to-noise ratio in modalities such as electroencephalography, which requires multiple trials to reliably decode user intentions. This induces a speed-accuracy trade-off, whereby higher accuracy comes at the cost of speed. The speed-accuracy balance is application-dependent, motivating controllable trade-offs. Conventional metrics, such as the Information Transfer Rate, combine speed and accuracy obscuring their dependence and potentially introducing biases. In this study, we propose an evaluation framework independent of classifier, paradigm, and early-stopping strategy that separates speed and accuracy. We employ two measures, Gain (relative speed improvement) and Conservation (relative accuracy preservation), and combine them into a tunable Gain-Cons Balance controlled by α, regulating the speed-accuracy trade-off. The parameter adjusts the operating point without modifying the classifier, facilitating deployment across scenarios. The framework was evaluated on P300 event-related potential paradigms using public recordings from 63 subjects as well as multiple classifiers and early-stopping strategies to achieve distinct operating points in speed-accuracy and bitrate. Results show that tuning α yields fast, accurate, or balanced BCI behaviours, demonstrating explicit control of the speed-accuracy trade-off. The method supports subject-level performance prediction and improves explainability of BCI behaviour. Further analysis of the Information Transfer Rate reveals a systematic bias toward speed, explained by the proposed framework through the Gain and Conservation measurements. Overall, this work establishes the speed-accuracy trade-off as a controllable design variable validated on public P300-based paradigms, enabling transparent evaluation and application-specific optimization of BCIs.

title: Motif-based morphology signatures for interpretable ECG screening and monitoring
comments: Accepted to the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Conference (EMBC) 2026
summary: Electrocardiography (ECG) remains central to cardiovascular screening, yet interpretation remains largely manual and episodic. Clinical practice relies on brief resting ECGs and, when required, long-duration ambulatory recordings, both generating data that require resource-intensive review. Consequently, subtle morphological changes or progressive drift preceding clinically apparent abnormalities may go unnoticed. We propose a motif-based framework that defines beat-aligned ECG motifs as interpretable cardiac signatures and quantifies morphological drift and deviation across short and long-term monitoring. Motifs are representative cardiac cycles capturing dominant morphology. We introduce three interpretable drift metrics: deviation from a normal sinus rhythm (NSR), deviation from a personalised baseline, and a motif instability index. Motifs are extracted by selecting beats that minimise Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) distance within fixed windows. We evaluate these metrics on short (PTB-XL) and long-duration (MIT-BIH Arrhythmia) ECG datasets. Interpretability is achieved through representative motif overlays and fiducial-based visualisations, enabling direct inspection of morphological changes. In MIT-BIH, the proposed metrics significantly separated predominantly normal from arrhythmic subjects (p<0.01). In PTB-XL, NSR deviation distinguished normal from abnormal ECGs across major diagnostic subtypes (p<1e-4, Cliff's delta up to 0.93). ECG motifs provide an interpretable representation of cardiac morphology, supporting scalable longitudinal monitoring and early detection of morphology-driven change.
comment: Accepted to the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Conference (EMBC) 2026

title: Project SPARROW and the Future of Conservation Technology
summary:
Global biodiversity is declining at unprecedented rates, yet the tools available to monitor and protect ecosystems remain limited by constraints in power, connectivity, and accessibility. We present SPARROW, a hardware and software open-source platform that integrates solar energy, edge artificial intelligence, and satellite communication to enable continuous, autonomous biodiversity monitoring in remote environments. Each SPARROW node combines a low-power Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) with modular visual, acoustic, and environmental sensors, performing on-device deep learning inference and transmitting summarized results through Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellite or Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) networks.
  We deployed SPARROW across tropical, temperate, and montane ecosystems in Colombia, Peru, Tanzania, and the United States, where it sustained 24/7 operation under variable environmental conditions and collected more than two million images and acoustic recordings in the first 190 days. The system demonstrated robust real-time classification and adaptive power management, achieving full autonomy without on-site human intervention. By integrating renewable energy, on-edge AI, and open-source design, SPARROW lowers the technical and financial barriers to ecological monitoring and establishes a scalable foundation for a distributed, intelligent network of sensors, an emerging "Internet of Living Things" for planetary biodiversity monitoring.

title: ChWDTA: Channel-wise Wavelet-Domain Transformer Attention and Entropy Modeling for Learned Image Compression
summary: State-of-the-art learned image compression (LIC) schemes are increasingly based on hybrid CNN-transformer architectures. To further improve rate-distortion performance, we introduce channel-wise wavelet transforms into both the transformer and entropy-coding components. First, we propose a channel-wise wavelet-domain transformer attention (ChWDTA) mechanism. ChWDTA keeps the efficient windowed spatial self-attention used in modern LIC backbones, but computes the Q/K/V projections on channel-wise wavelet-transformed features before mapping the attention output back with the inverse transform. The resulting Channel-wise Wavelet-Domain Transformer Block (ChWDTB) therefore preserves the spatial tokenization pattern of windowed attention while sparsifying the channel covariance seen by the attention projections. Second, in the entropy-coding stage, we introduce a channel-wise wavelet packet (ChWP) decomposition that produces four equal-sized subbands, which better fit channel-wise slice-based autoregressive entropy modeling. When each channel-wise subband is divided into two slices, we use eight slices for entropy coding. With this configuration, the proposed scheme obtains BD-rate reductions of -17.82%, -19.15%, and -22.56% on the Kodak, CLIC Professional Validation, and Tecnick test sets, respectively. Even when each channel-wise subband is coded as a single slice, the scheme still retains most of the coding gains with lower complexity. The results confirm the advantage of introducing wavelet transform in CNN-transformer-based LIC schemes.

title: SpikeWFM: Spiking-Aided Wireless Foundation Model for Robust Channel Prediction
summary: This paper proposes SpikeWFM, a novel hybrid architecture that integrates spiking neural networks (SNNs) with conventional artificial neural network (ANN)-based transformers for wireless foundation models (WFMs). Inspired by the noise-robust and energy-efficient information processing in the human brain, SpikeWFM aims to enhance the resilience of WFMs against noise and interference while maintaining strong generalization capabilities across diverse wireless scenarios. Drawing from the success of large language models, WFMs leverage self-supervised pre-training on large-scale datasets spanning various wireless environments to learn a unified embedding that supports a wide range of downstream tasks, including channel prediction, channel estimation, beam predition, positioning and etc. Such models typically outperform task-specific designs and exhibit superior adaptability to unseen conditions. However, existing WFMs remain vulnerable to realistic noise and interference in practical wireless systems. To address this limitation, we incorporate spiking neurons into the transformer-based WFM architecture. We provide a brief theoretical analysis demonstrating how the SNN-ANN hybrid effectively mitigates noise and interference through temporal sparsity and event-driven processing. Experimental results show that SpikeWFM consistently outperforms conventional ANN-based WFMs in both pre-training convergence and channel prediction accuracy. Additional results on communication and sensing tasks will be presented in the full journal version of this work.

title: Mathematical framework for perception-driven parameter choice in image denoising
summary: We approach image denoising from a perception-driven perspective: how can we select the parameters that are best suited for human visual perception? We combine research methods in mathematics and psychology to develop a mathematical framework for measuring perceived similarity. We construct a sample set of differently denoised photographs by using the same base image as input data and by tuning the parameter value in a total variation denoising algorithm. A comparison test is conducted with human participants to survey perceived differences between the images. Analyzing the results with psychometric scaling provides us with a HaarPSI value to use as a threshold in discretizing parameter grids. As a result, we obtain psychometrically scaled, openly available image sets that are ready to use in further experiments in perception-driven imaging, as well as a framework for ensuing experiments involving comparison tests.

title: Regime-Adaptive Continual Learning for Portfolio Management
summary: Financial markets are inherently non-stationary, exhibiting frequent regime shifts and structural changes that render traditional Portfolio Management (PM) approaches ineffective. Existing remedies, such as rolling-window retraining and naive online fine-tuning, are hindered by high computational costs and insufficient knowledge utilization, respectively, resulting in low returns and limited adaptability. Continual learning (CL) offers a promising paradigm by enabling trading agents to accumulate and transfer knowledge across sequential tasks. In this paper, we propose \textbf{Re}gime-aware \textbf{C}ontinual \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{P}ortfolio management (\textbf{ReCAP}), a novel framework that integrates CL into PM to address the challenges of dynamic financial environments. ReCAP employs an adaptive regime detection module to segment historical market data into variable-length regimes, enabling regime-specific learning of policy vectors and the construction of a policy library. During continual trading, a regime-gate module adaptively combines policy vectors from the library based on the current market state, facilitating rapid adaptation to newly detected regimes. Only the regime-gate and the current regime's policy vector are continually updated to preserve useful knowledge effectively. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets demonstrate that ReCAP consistently outperforms popular baselines, achieving superior returns in long-term investment horizons and rapid adaptation to regime shifts.

title: Multi-Contrast MRI Motion Correction via Parameter-Informed Disentanglement and Adaptive Experts
summary: Motion artifacts in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) degrade diagnostic reliability. Existing deep learning methods are typically contrast-specific and fail to generalize across diverse modalities and artifact severities. We propose a unified framework combining parameter-informed contrast disentanglement with severity-aware adaptive correction. ScanCLIP, pretrained on over 30,000 MRI text-image pairs, derives contrast embeddings from acquisition parameters to disentangle contrast style from anatomical content, yielding contrast-free features. A Vision Transformer then estimates motion severity and routes features through a Mixture-of-Experts network, enabling targeted artifact correction. A dual-pathway decoder reconstructs both the clean image and residual artifact map, enforcing image-space consistency. On IXI and HCP benchmarks, our method improves PSNR by 0.75 dB and SSIM by up to 0.0279 over state-of-the-art approaches, with larger gains at higher artifact severities. It further demonstrates robust zero-shot generalization on real-world clinical data acquired with unseen scanning parameters, where existing methods either fail to remove artifacts or introduce additional distortions.

title: A physics-informed foundation model for quantitative diffusion MRI
summary: Understanding the human brain requires access to its microscopic tissue architecture. Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides the only noninvasive window into whole-brain microstructure in vivo, yet reliable quantitative mapping remains confined to specialized research settings requiring dense sampling and optimized acquisition protocols. To address this gap, we present a physics-informed generative microstructure network (PIGMENT) that learns a universal generative prior of human brain microstructure and adapts it zero-shot to each participant's measured data to recover subject-specific maps. Trained on 11375 scans spanning multiple sites, vendors, and field strengths, PIGMENT enabled reliable quantitative mapping for tensor, kurtosis, and NODDI models across external datasets from five independent centers. It remains effective where conventional fitting becomes unreliable, recovering meaningful maps from extremely sparse acquisitions while supporting downstream tractography and structural connectivity mapping. PIGMENT estimates demonstrated strong biological validity, preserving submillimeter cortical microarchitectural patterns and early-childhood white matter developmental trajectories from 10-fold accelerated scans. Furthermore, PIGMENT enables reliable quantitative tensor mapping on cost-efficient low-field systems and the extraction of tumor-related biomarkers using ultra-fast clinical protocols. Together, these results establish PIGMENT as a physics-informed foundation model that extends quantitative diffusion MRI into regimes traditionally too sparse, heterogeneous, or clinically constrained for reliable analysis.

title: Interpreting FCDNNs via RG on Exponential Family
summary: We consider establishing the interpretability theory of deep learning through constructing a corresponding relationship between the renormalization group (RG) method in statistical physics and the training process of deep neural networks (DNNs). We have proved the constructed relationship using the one-dimensional Ising model as the input data. In this paper we generalize our results to the case of continuous input data, which is a necessary preparation for applying the corresponding framework to real-world data. To be representative, we consider a class of data distribution in the exponential family. We prove that when the parameters of fully connected (FC) DNNs achieve their optimal value after training, the characteristic parameters of the feature layer output of DNNs are equal to the fixed points of the characteristic parameters of input data under RG method for continuous fields. This conclusion shows that the training process of DNNs is equivalent to RG calculation on this kind of data and therefore the network can extract main features from the input data just like RG. Also, the equivalence further validates the correspondence framework we have established, providing an explanation for the outstanding performance of DNNs on real-world data.

title: Training-Free Continuous Bitrate Control for Scalable Image Coding for Humans and Machines
summary: Continuous variable-rate compression is highly demanded in real-world applications, but remains underexplored in scalable image coding for humans and machines. In this paper, we propose a training-free variable-rate scalable image coding framework. By adjusting quantization steps based on predicted scale values, the proposed method achieves continuous bitrate control while preserving high-scale information in the machine and enhancement layers. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and highlight the importance of bitrate allocation between the two layers.

title: 21cmEMUv3: a hybrid diffusion-LSTM emulator of 21cmFAST summary observables
summary: We are witnessing a surge in observations of the cosmic dawn (CD) and epoch of reionisation (EoR), driving an increasing demand for fast and robust theoretical interpretation frameworks. In response, machine learning (ML), and emulation in particular, has emerged as a powerful approach to accelerate and enhance inference pipelines. In this work, we present 21cmEMUv3, an emulator trained on 21cmFASTv3 simulations that model both atomically and molecularly cooling galaxies. 21cmEMUv3 is conditioned on $σ_8$ and ten astrophysical parameters to produce seven summary observables: (i) the cylindrical 21cm power spectrum (PS), emulated for the first time at such high resolution and accuracy across a wide redshift range of $z \sim$ 6--30; (ii) the spherically-averaged 21cm PS; (iii) the mean neutral fraction of the intergalactic medium (IGM); (iv) the mean 21cm spin temperature; (v) the global 21cm signal; (vi) the ultraviolet (UV) luminosity functions (LFs); and (vii) the Thomson scattering optical depth. Notably, the cylindrical 21cm PS is emulated via score-based diffusion, while the remaining six summaries are emulated via long-short term memory (LSTM) networks, all achieving sub-percent median accuracy. We use the emulator to reinterpret current 21cm PS upper limits from HERA, for the first time using state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations to inform priors on star formation inside molecularly cooling galaxies. We find that our inferred soft-band X-ray luminosity per unit star formation rate is consistent with extrapolations of high-mass X-ray binaries to the low-metallicity regimes expected in the first galaxies, excluding values below $10^{39.2}$ erg s$^{-1}M^{-1}_\odot \rm{yr}$ at $95\%$ confidence. Finally, we produce forecasts for the detection of the cosmic 21cm PS with the Square Kilometre Array for different array configurations. The 21cmEMU package is publicly available.

title: Civilizational Metamaterials: Engineering Coordination Under Capability Gradients and Structural Turbulence
comments: 19 pages, 4 figures. Accepted for presentation at AGI-26 (Springer LNAI, forthcoming). v2 corrects the sign of the synergy term in the constitutive law (Eq. 2) and reformulates H3 as a threshold-crossing claim, per peer review
summary: We argue that governance must transition from a normative discipline to an engineering discipline, and we develop a formal framework, inspired by the physics of metamaterials, to make this transition quantitative and testable. Artificial General Intelligence affects civilization primarily by increasing decision velocity while human verification capacity remains bounded. When the cost of validating AI-generated outputs exceeds the expected utility of acting on them, rational agents default to inaction: a stable but catastrophic Nash equilibrium we term the Freezing Equilibrium. Drawing on metamaterials, where emergent macro-properties arise from designed microstructure, we develop a phenomenological constitutive law for institutional coordination: $R_{\mathrm{eff}} = β\cdot (1-ρ) \cdot (1-τ) \cdot (1-γρτ)$, where $β$ is the decision branching factor, $ρ$ is provenance fidelity, $τ$ is the verification rate, and $γ\in [0,1]$ captures correlated-detection synergy between provenance and verification failures. The model predicts a sharp phase transition between self-healing ($R_{\mathrm{eff}} < 1$) and self-destabilizing ($R_{\mathrm{eff}} > 1$) regimes. We introduce a three-class provenance taxonomy: cryptographic, institutional, and context binding, and derive four falsifiable hypotheses with a proposed 12-week stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial in government grant review panels. The framework bridges AI alignment theory and institutional design.

title: Further evidence towards the Fourier Entropy-Influence conjecture
summary: The Fourier Entropy-Influence (FEI) conjecture states that the Fourier entropy of Boolean functions is uniformly bounded by their total influence. It has been verified for canonical examples such as disjoint tribes and for some classes of Boolean functions such as symmetric functions and read-$k$ decision trees (with a constant that depends linearly on $k$). In this note we present new classes of Boolean functions that verify the FEI conjecture. The key element is an inequality controlling the difference between the entropy of a function $f$ and the average of the entropies of $f^{\pm}$, the sub-functions obtained by setting $x_m=\pm1$ for some $m$, by the $m$-influence of $f$. If this key inequality were to hold for Boolean functions, then the full FEI conjecture would follow by induction. We introduce the notion of a stopping binary tree and observe that functions that satisfy the key inequality at the branching nodes of the tree and the FEI conjecture at the stopping nodes will satisfy the FEI conjecture. We identify some classes of functions that fit this framework and, along the way, demonstrate some results that we hope the experts in this fascinating field might find useful.

title: An Upper Bound on Grothendieck's Constant
summary: We show that Grothendieck's real constant $K_G$ can be upper bounded by projecting vectors onto a random plane through the origin and thresholding a degree five Hermite polynomial. This resolves a conjecture of Braverman-Makarychev-Makarychev-Naor from 2011, who required an extra randomization step in their rounding scheme and proved $K_G<\fracπ{2\log(1+\sqrt{2})}-10^{-500}$. As a corollary of our result, we prove the bound $K_G<\fracπ{2\log(1+\sqrt{2})}-10^{-217}$ by thresholding degree three Hermite polynomials in the plane. We finally give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that $K_G<\fracπ{2\log(1+\sqrt{2})}-10^{-5}$ using interval arithmetic and degree three Hermite polynomial thresholding.

title: Symmetry-Protected Quantum Computing using Metamaterials
comments: Invited talk at META (International conference on Metamaterials, Photonic Crystals and Plasmonics), Dublin, July 14-17, 2026
summary: We propose a new architecture for practical quantum computing that combines three established principles: symmetry protection of relative-motion qubits via the generalized Kohn theorem, control via twisted-light orbital angular momentum, and metamaterial nanofocusing (e.g. using Weyl-semimetal plasmonics). Crucially, the core mechanism is generic: it applies to any current or future quantum computing system involving parabolic confinement, including cold atoms, ions, and semiconductor dots.
comment: Invited talk at META (International conference on Metamaterials, Photonic Crystals and Plasmonics), Dublin, July 14-17, 2026

title: ReFLEX: Length-Generalizable CSI Denoising for MIMO-OFDM via Relative-Frequency Bias
comments: 5 pages, 3 figures, submitted to IEEE journal
summary: This letter studies CSI denoising for MIMO--OFDM with variable NR resource block (RB) allocations. ReFLEX is a length-generalizable Transformer whose frequency attention uses a relative-frequency position bias (RFPB) generated from subcarrier offsets. A single checkpoint handles unseen RB lengths and can be applied to sparse DM-RS observations in the tested RB5/RB10 PUSCH setup without retraining. In a 3GPP~TR~38.901 UMa NLOS channel, ReFLEX achieves about $-9.6$~dB NMSE on unseen RB lengths. In NR PUSCH/UL-SCH simulations, ReFLEX denoising followed by time-frequency interpolation reduces the 10\% BLER threshold by about 2--3~dB.
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, submitted to IEEE journal

title: Out-of-Distribution generalization of quantile regression with heavy tailed inputs: an SVM approach
summary:
We study quantile regression in an extrapolation regime where the covariate takes unusually large values. Under regular variation assumptions, extreme observations can be effectively characterized through their angular components, enabling learning strategies that focus on the angle of the most extreme observations. This approach is formalized through the minimization of an asymptotic conditional risk that localizes learning in the tail of the covariate distribution.
  We propose a novel Support Vector Machine (SVM) framework for extreme quantile regression, leveraging reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to handle high-dimensional and nonlinear settings. Our method also accommodates unbounded response variables and avoids restrictive transformations. We establish finite-sample learning guarantees under mild regularity assumptions.
  The proposed framework unifies ideas from statistical learning and multivariate extremes, providing a tractable and theoretically grounded approach to extrapolation. We complement our theoretical findings with an empirical study on river flow data from the Danube, demonstrating the practical relevance of our methods.

title: Flow Matching for Convective-Scale Precipitation Downscaling
summary: Generative machine learning is an increasingly important complement to dynamical downscaling for producing high-resolution precipitation projections, with diffusion models currently the leading approach. Flow matching is a related generative framework that has recently achieved strong results across image, video and other domains, and shown early promise for downscaling. We train a flow matching model to map daily precipitation from 8 km to 2 km over a convective-scale domain centred on Singapore, and benchmark it against CPMGEM, a score-based diffusion model. Flow matching achieves consistently better spatial skill: higher fractions skill score at every precipitation threshold and neighbourhood scale tested, and tighter structure and amplitude components of the SAL score with comparable location skill. However, flow matching underestimates the upper tail of the precipitation distribution, resulting in a dry bias in the climatological mean. These results suggest that flow matching is a competitive generative framework for convective-scale precipitation downscaling, particularly well suited to capturing spatial structure.

title: Is Zero-Shot Super-Resolution Possible in Operator Learning?
summary: Neural operators are often reported to exhibit zero-shot super-resolution, a phenomenon in which a model trained on coarse grids produces accurate predictions on finer testing grids without additional retraining. Despite strong empirical evidence, the theoretical foundations of this phenomenon remain unclear. In this work, we provide a systematic theoretical study of zero-shot super-resolution in operator learning. We first show that zero-shot super-resolution can be information-theoretically impossible even in benign settings such as when the input functions are available over the entire continuum and the ground truth is a simple rank-one linear operator. We then identify H{\" o}lder smoothness of the output functions as a sufficient condition for zero-shot super-resolution and derive corresponding generalization bounds. Finally, we also validate the identified failure modes through experimental results.

title: ERICA: Quantifying Replicability of Cluster Analysis
summary: Despite being ubiquitous in science, clustering remains a technique whose results are not quantitatively scrutinized via a framework. We present an analysis called evaluating replicability via iterative clustering assignments (ERICA) that is applied to a dataset to determine whether clusters are identified in a replicable manner. The pipeline computes a statistic that describes whether structure is found in a dataset. Quantitative visualization methods are presented to answer important questions such as the similarity between clusters, and the identity of points that may be outliers. When tested on synthetic data, the findings show clusters being discovered in a replicable manner. However, we note a possibility for non-replicable results when the pipeline is applied to three gene expression datasets for breast cancer subtype validation. The study underscores the need for rigorous inspection and offers a practical tool for doing so.

title: Cluster Analysis with Resampling for Validation and Exploration (CARVE)
summary: Clustering is widely used across the sciences as the foundation for downstream data-driven scientific discoveries. However, clustering results are highly sensitive to the choice of algorithm, preprocessing, and the number of clusters $k$, producing scientific claims that are often not reproducible. The current state of the art for validating clustering solutions consists of clustering validation indices (CVIs) such as Silhouette, Davies-Bouldin, and Calinski-Harabasz, which rely on geometric assumptions that break down on the heavy-tailed, high-dimensional, and nonlinearly structured data encountered in biomedical research. Resampling-based alternatives - grounded in the ideas of clustering stability and generalizability - have been proposed but remain scattered across specialized tools with no unified, accessible software. We fill this gap with CARVE (Cluster Analysis with Resampling for Validation and Exploration), an open-source Python and R package that jointly evaluates multiple clustering algorithms and hyperparameters, returning stability and generalizability diagnostics at the global, cluster, and sample level together with principled selection rules and consensus-based cluster labels. Across six synthetic benchmarks CARVE consistently recovers near-optimal clusterings where classical indices degrade substantially. On experimental genomics and proteomics data sets, CARVE recovers finer biological structure when classical CVIs collapse entirely. CARVE is available with a scikit-learn-compatible Python API and an analogous R interface compatible with Seurat workflows.

title: Empirical Approximation of $L_p$ Norms
summary:
We study empirical $L_p$ moments of a random vector $\pmb\varphi$ based on its i.i.d.\ copies $\pmb\varphi^1,\ldots,\pmb\varphi^m$, that is, $\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m |\langle \pmb\varphi^j,y\rangle|^p$. Our main result is a new estimate for the expected uniform deviation \[ \mathbb{E}\sup_{y\in D}\biggl| \frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m |\langle \pmb\varphi^j,y\rangle|^p -\mathbb{E}|\langle \pmb\varphi,y\rangle|^p \biggr| \] over an arbitrary index set $D$. The proof is based on a new bound for Talagrand's $γ$-functional, sharper than the standard Dudley-type entropy estimate. We then apply this estimate to the following two problems.
  First, for $p>2$, we study Marcinkiewicz-type discretization of $L_p$ norms on an $N$-dimensional subspace $X_N\subset B(Ω)$ of bounded functions on a probability space $(Ω,μ)$. We obtain bounds in terms of the norm of the embedding $
(X_N,\|\cdot\|_{L_p(μ)})\hookrightarrow B(Ω). $
In particular, we prove that when this norm is of order $N^{1/p}$ and \[ m \ge C(p)\, N\log N\,(\log\log N)^{p-1}, \] then $m$ random samples suffice to approximate the $L_p(μ)$ norm uniformly on $X_N$ by the sampled discrete $L_p$ norm. This substantially improves the previously known bound in this setting $
m \ge C(p)\, N(\log N)^{\min\{p,3\}}, $
and is optimal up to the factor $(\log\log N)^{p-1}$ in the random-sampling setting.
  Second, for $1\le p<2$, we obtain an $L_p$ analogue of the restricted isometry property via random sampling for bounded orthogonal systems and, more generally, for $N$-element systems $\mathcal D_N$ satisfying a Riesz-type condition. We prove that when \[ m \ge C(p)\, s\log N\,(\log s)^2\,\log\log s, \] then $m$ random samples suffice to guarantee an $L_p$ restricted isometry-type property uniformly over the class of all $s$-sparse functions generated by $\mathcal D_N$.

title: Clustering-enhanced adaptive Benders decomposition for energy systems planning optimization
summary: High-resolution energy system capacity expansion models (CEMs) for energy transition planning often result in large-scale mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations. Benders decomposition (BD) offers a scalable solution approach by iteratively solving a master problem (MP) for investment decisions and multiple subproblems (SPs) for operational decisions. However, accumulated Benders cuts generated by the SPs can make MP solution a major computational bottleneck. Incomplete SP parallelization can also introduce further bottlenecks when SPs exceed available CPUs. We develop clustering-enhanced BD methods to address these challenges, by using clustering to group similar SPs for: a) aggregated Benders cut construction and b) identification of representative SPs to be solved most frequently. For grouped-cuts, we examine two adaptive formulations based on dual variables and a fixed-grouping formulation based on exogenous time-series inputs. We evaluate these methods in an electricity-sector CEM across varying system sizes, temporal SP lengths, inter-SP coupling strengths represented by CO2 policy, computational resources, and stochastic settings. Relative to a benchmark regularized multi-cut formulation, adaptive grouped cuts outperform fixed grouping and provide substantial benefits under weak inter-temporal coupling. The largest gains occur in larger systems with shorter SP horizons, where the MP accounts for a greater share of runtime. Their effectiveness declines under strong inter-temporal coupling, such as annual CO2 emissions limits, where the benchmark multi-cut performs best. The representative-SP method outperforms the benchmark under limited parallelization when SP solution dominates runtime. Overall, the preferred BD strategy depends on inter-SP coupling strength and whether computational burden lies in the MP or the SPs.

title: AutoIQ: An Ensemble Framework for Automatic Assessment of Geometric Distortion in Prostate Diffusion-Weighted Imaging
summary: Geometric distortion in prostate diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) can impair lesion localization and reduce the reliability of MRI-based clinical assessment. We propose AutoIQ, an ensemble machine learning framework for automatic quantification and classification of DWI geometric distortion severity. A total of 140 retrospective prostate biparametric MRI examinations were analyzed, including 33 scans with severe distortion requiring repeat acquisition and 107 scans with acceptable distortion based on expert radiologist assessment. AutoIQ combines two complementary distortion quantification strategies: a segmentation-based method measuring prostate boundary mismatch between T2-weighted imaging (T2WI) and DWI, and a registration-based method estimating deformation magnitude after DWI-to-T2WI alignment. The resulting distortion scores were used to train individual classifiers and a logistic-regression ensemble model. Both computational methods significantly differentiated severe from acceptable distortion cases (p < 0.001). On an independent test set, the ensemble model achieved an accuracy of 0.95, F1-score of 0.93, and AUC of 0.98, outperforming individual models. These results suggest that AutoIQ can provide automated, quantitative quality assessment for prostate DWI and may help identify scans that require repeat acquisition.

title: Data-Driven Spectral Prediction for Accelerating Large-Scale Electronic Structure Calculations
summary: Simulating large molecular systems comprising thousands of atoms requires highly scalable methodologies. While modern Density Functional Theory (DFT) codes exhibit linear scaling, solving the associated large, sparse generalized eigenproblems remains a critical computational bottleneck on exascale architectures. In the context of the LimitX project, we propose a data-driven framework to accelerate these calculations. By shifting the machine learning target from discrete eigenvalues to the coefficients of an interpolating Chebyshev polynomial, and by comparing both all-atom and fragment-based structural representations, we successfully overcome the dimensionality constraints of large-scale spectral prediction. We investigate three machine learning models (Kernel Ridge Regression, Graph Neural Networks, and Random Forests) trained on a novel 2 TB dataset of protein dimers. The predicted spectra provide initial guesses that effectively bypass early Self-Consistent Field (SCF) iterations in BigDFT. Ultimately, these spectral predictors will be deployed to dynamically optimize upcoming rational filter-based eigensolvers, such as FrASE, which is currently in initial development.

AI.title_translation: 数据驱动的光谱预测用于加速大规模电子结构计算
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种通过预测切比雪夫多项式系数来预测大规模分子光谱的数据驱动框架，能有效绕过BigDFT中早期的自洽场迭代，从而加速大规模电子结构计算。
AI.motivation: 在百亿亿次（exascale）计算架构上，求解大型、稀疏的广义特征值问题是线性标度密度泛函理论（DFT）计算中的关键计算瓶颈，限制了数千原子规模的大型分子系统的模拟效率。
AI.method: 提出一个数据驱动的框架，将机器学习的目标从离散特征值转换为插值切比雪夫多项式的系数，并对比了全原子和基于片段的结构表征。在新型2 TB蛋白质二聚体数据集上，训练并评估了三种机器学习模型：核岭回归（KRR）、图神经网络（GNN）和随机森林（RF）。
AI.result: 成功克服了大规模光谱预测的维度限制。预测的光谱提供了优异的初始猜测，能够有效绕过BigDFT中早期的自洽场（SCF）迭代，从而加速计算。
AI.conclusion: 数据驱动的光谱预测器能够提供高质量的初始猜测，有效加速BigDFT中的SCF收敛，并将在未来用于动态优化基于有理滤波器的特征值求解器（如FrASE）。
AI.translation: 模拟包含数千个原子的大型分子系统需要高度可扩展的方法。虽然现代密度泛函理论（DFT）程序表现出线性缩放特性，但在百亿亿次（exascale）架构上求解相关的大型、稀疏广义特征值问题仍然是一个关键的计算瓶颈。在 LimitX 项目的背景下，我们提出了一个数据驱动的框架来加速这些计算。通过将机器学习的目标从离散特征值转向插值切比雪夫多项式的系数，并对比全原子和基于片段的结构表征，我们成功克服了大规模光谱预测的维度限制。我们研究了在新型 2 TB 蛋白质二聚体数据集上训练的三种机器学习模型（核岭回归、图神经网络和随机森林）。预测的光谱提供了初始猜测，可有效绕过 BigDFT 中早期的自洽场（SCF）迭代。最终，这些光谱预测器将被部署用于动态优化即将推出的基于有理滤波器的特征值求解器，例如目前处于初步开发阶段的 FrASE。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一个在LimitX项目背景下的数据驱动框架，旨在加速大规模电子结构计算。该方法通过将机器学习预测目标从传统的离散特征值转变为切比雪夫插值多项式的系数，并结合全原子和片段结构表征，克服了维度限制。通过在2 TB蛋白质二聚体数据集上训练核岭回归、图神经网络和随机森林模型，该框架能够生成高质量的光谱预测作为初始猜测，从而在BigDFT中绕过早期的自洽场（SCF）迭代，并为未来优化新型特征值求解器提供支持。
AI.keywords: 电子结构计算, 密度泛函理论, 光谱预测, 切比雪夫多项式, 机器学习
AI.comments: 该论文创新地将机器学习的目标从预测离散特征值转变为预测切比雪夫插值多项式的系数，这一巧妙的设计成功避开了大规模光谱预测中的维度灾难。利用2 TB的蛋白质二聚体数据集进行训练，展示了该方法在实际生物大分子模拟中的巨大潜力。其局限性在于目前主要针对蛋白质二聚体数据进行了测试，对于其他类型材料或更广泛化学空间的泛化能力仍需进一步验证。

title: A Distribution-Free Framework for Rewrite-Based Human-text Detection via Knockoff Filtering
summary: We propose a distribution-free statistical framework that converts arbitrary rewrite-based detectors into detectors with finite-sample FDR guarantees without retraining. Our key observation is that rewrite-based detection implicitly constructs knockoff samples, enabling LLM-generated text detection to be formulated as a multiple hypothesis testing problem with knockoff structure. This perspective separates the design of detection statistics from the control of false discoveries, allowing existing rewrite detectors to inherit finite-sample false discovery rate (FDR) guarantees through a simple calibration procedure. We demonstrate reliable FDR control with meaningful detection power across three detection models, 19 domains, and four LLMs.

AI.title_translation: 基于Knockoff滤波的重写式人类文本检测无分布框架
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一个无分布统计框架，利用Knockoff滤波将现有的重写式LLM文本检测器转化为具有有限样本错误发现率（FDR）保证的检测器，且无需进行重新训练。
AI.motivation: 现有的LLM生成文本检测方法（特别是重写式检测器）缺乏对错误发现率（FDR）的有限样本理论保证，且在实际应用中往往需要重新训练模型以适应不同的分布。
AI.method: 提出一种无分布统计框架。其核心在于观察到重写式检测隐式地构建了knockoff（仿造）样本，从而将LLM生成文本的检测任务转化为具有knockoff结构的多重假设检验问题。通过简单的校准程序，该框架将检测统计量的设计与错误发现的控制相分离，使现有重写检测器无需重新训练即可获得有限样本FDR保证。
AI.result: 在3个检测模型、19个领域和4个大语言模型（LLM）的实验中，该框架展示了可靠的FDR控制能力，并保持了显著的检测效能（detection power）。
AI.conclusion: 该无分布框架成功地将任意重写式检测器转化为具有有限样本FDR保证的检测器，在不牺牲检测能力的前提下，实现了可靠的错误控制。
AI.translation: 我们提出了一个无分布的统计框架，该框架可以在无需重新训练的情况下，将任意基于重写的检测器转换为具有有限样本错误发现率（FDR）保证的检测器。我们的关键观察是，基于重写的检测隐式地构建了knockoff（仿造）样本，从而使大语言模型（LLM）生成的文本检测能够被公式化为具有knockoff结构的多重假设检验问题。这一视角将检测统计量的设计与错误发现的控制分离开来，使现有的重写检测器能够通过一个简单的校准程序继承有限样本FDR保证。我们在三个检测模型、19个领域和四个LLM上展示了可靠的FDR控制和有意义的检测能力。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种用于重写式大语言模型（LLM）生成文本检测的无分布统计框架。该框架利用Knockoff滤波的思想，将重写式检测过程转化为多重假设检验问题。通过简单的校准，现有的重写检测器无需重新训练即可获得有限样本错误发现率（FDR）的理论保证。实验证明了其在多模型、多领域下的可靠性和检测能力。
AI.keywords: 人类文本检测, Knockoff滤波, 错误发现率 (FDR), 无分布框架, 大语言模型 (LLMs)
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地将统计学中的Knockoff滤波方法与LLM文本检测相结合。其最大亮点在于“无分布”且“无需重新训练”，能够直接赋能现有的重写式检测器，使其获得坚实的有限样本错误发现率（FDR）理论保证。这在实际应用中对于控制误报（将人类文本误判为AI文本）至关重要。局限性在于该方法主要针对“基于重写”的检测器，对于其他类型的检测器的适用性或泛化能力仍有待进一步探索。

title: Riemannian Stochastic Optimization for Sufficient Dimension Reduction
summary: Sufficient dimension reduction (SDR) makes high-dimensional regression tractable by projecting the covariates onto a low-dimensional subspace that preserves the conditional mean of the response. Existing gradient-based estimators either operate in the ambient space and suffer from the curse of dimensionality, or localize in the reduced space at a per-outer-iteration cost at least quadratic in the sample size. We show that minimizers of the population Minimum Average Variance Estimation (MAVE) risk approximate the same Grassmannian target as the Outer Product of Gradients (OPG), and recast the empirical criterion as a smooth maximization on the Stiefel manifold with closed-form Riemannian gradient. The resulting algorithm, SMAVE, combines sparse projected-space nearest-neighbor localization with Riemannian stochastic gradient ascent. A simplified version comes with almost-sure convergence and a non-asymptotic rate matching the standard non-convex stochastic first-order scaling. Empirically, SMAVE matches or improves on RMAVE's synthetic subspace recovery at moderate-to-high ambient dimension, and on four real datasets it uniformly improves over OPG and is competitive with or outperforms RMAVE at orders of magnitude lower runtime.

AI.title_translation: 用于充分维度约简的黎曼随机优化
AI.tldr: 本文提出了 SMAVE 算法，通过将充分维度约简问题重构为 Stiefel 流形上的光滑最大化，并结合黎曼随机梯度上升，实现了在计算时间降低几个数量级的同时保持极高的降维精度和理论收敛保证。
AI.motivation: 现有的基于梯度的充分维度约简（SDR）估计器存在局限性：要么在环境空间中操作并遭受维数灾难，要么在简化空间中进行局部化，导致每次外迭代的计算成本至少与样本量呈二次方关系，难以应对大规模高维数据。
AI.method: 证明了总体最小平均方差估计（MAVE）风险的极小值点逼近与梯度外积（OPG）相同的格拉斯曼目标，并将经验准则重构为 Stiefel 流形上的光滑最大化问题，推导出闭式黎曼梯度。基于此，提出了 SMAVE 算法，该算法将稀疏投影空间最近邻定位与黎曼随机梯度上升相结合。其简化版本具有几乎处处收敛性，并具有与标准非凸随机一阶标度相匹配的非渐近收敛率。
AI.result: 实验表明，在中高维环境维度下，SMAVE 在合成子空间恢复上的表现达到或优于 RMAVE。在四个真实数据集上，SMAVE 的预测性能一致优于 OPG，且在运行时间比 RMAVE 低几个数量级的情况下，其表现与 RMAVE 相当或更优。
AI.conclusion: SMAVE 是一种高效、可扩展且具有坚实理论收敛保证的充分维度约简方法，能够在大规模高维数据集上实现快速且准确的子空间恢复。
AI.translation: 充分维度约简（SDR）通过将协变量投影到保留响应条件均值的低维子空间上，使得高维回归变得可行。现有的基于梯度的估计器要么在环境空间中运行并受到维数灾难的影响，要么在减少的空间中进行局部化，其每次外迭代的成本至少与样本量呈二次方关系。我们表明，总体最小平均方差估计（MAVE）风险的极小值点逼近与梯度外积（OPG）相同的格拉斯曼目标，并将经验准则重构为 Stiefel 流形上的光滑最大化问题，具有闭式黎曼梯度。由此产生的算法 SMAVE 将稀疏投影空间最近邻定位与黎曼随机梯度上升相结合。一个简化版本具有几乎处处收敛性以及与标准非凸随机一阶标度相匹配的非渐近速率。在实证方面，SMAVE 在中高环境维度下的合成子空间恢复上达到或改进了 RMAVE，并且在四个真实数据集上，它一致优于 OPG，且在运行时间低几个数量级的情况下与 RMAVE 相当或更优。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为 SMAVE 的新型充分维度约简算法。该方法通过将 MAVE 风险重构为 Stiefel 流形上的光滑最大化问题，并结合稀疏投影空间最近邻定位与黎曼随机梯度上升，克服了传统方法计算复杂度高或受维数灾难影响的缺陷。SMAVE 具有几乎处处收敛性和非渐近速率保证，在保证高精度的同时极大地降低了计算时间。
AI.keywords: 充分维度约简, 黎曼随机优化, Stiefel 流形, 最小平均方差估计, 随机梯度上升
AI.comments: 该论文成功地将流形优化（特别是黎曼随机梯度上升）与充分维度约简（MAVE）相结合，有效解决了传统 MAVE 方法在大样本和高维情况下的计算瓶颈。其提出的 SMAVE 算法不仅在理论上具有几乎处处收敛性和非渐近收敛率保证，而且在实验中展现出比 RMAVE 低几个数量级的运行时间，具有极高的实用价值和理论创新性。

title: Parameter-Free and Group Conditional Online Conformal Prediction
summary: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is critical for the deployment of machine learning predictors in real-world scenarios where the data distribution may shift over time (i.e., data may not be exchangeable). Online conformal prediction (OCP) methods address this issue at the expense of either (i) group-wise error control or (ii) learning-rate independent implementation. Group-conditional coverage is essential for fairness across different collections of data points and for providing finer UQ guarantees. Parameter-free optimization is crucial for robustness to adversarial and unknown data shifts. We propose a parameter-free algorithm for group-conditional OCP and demonstrate that it achieves the best group-conditional coverage guarantees.We evaluate our algorithm on synthetic and real-world data, demonstrating that our method not only improves the reliability of existing parameter-free OCP methods but also provides prediction intervals that are comparable in size to well-tuned group-conditional approaches. By unifying group-conditional coverage with parameter-free online algorithms, our work lays a foundation for fair and robust uncertainty quantification in shifting environments.

AI.title_translation: 无参数且分组条件的在线共形预测
AI.tldr: 本文提出了一种无参数的分组条件在线共形预测算法，在数据分布偏移环境下同时实现了鲁棒的无参数优化与公平的分组条件覆盖。
AI.motivation: 在现实世界的非可交换数据流（数据分布随时间偏移）中，现有在线共形预测方法无法同时实现“分组误差控制（保证公平性与精细不确定性量化）”与“无参数实现（保证对未知和对抗性偏移的鲁棒性）”。为此，需要一种兼具两者的算法。
AI.method: 提出了一种用于分组条件在线共形预测（OCP）的无参数算法，该算法将分组条件覆盖与无参数在线算法相统一。
AI.result: 在合成和真实数据上的实验表明，该算法不仅提高了现有无参数在线共形预测方法的可靠性，实现了最佳的分组条件覆盖保证，而且其生成的预测区间大小与经过精心调优的分组条件方法相当。
AI.conclusion: 本研究通过将分组条件覆盖与无参数在线算法相统一，成功解决了分布偏移环境下不确定性量化的公平性与鲁棒性问题，为构建可靠的机器学习预测系统奠定了基础。
AI.translation: 不确定性量化（UQ）对于机器学习预测器在实际场景（其中数据分布可能会随时间发生偏移，即数据可能不满足可交换性）中的部署至关重要。在线共形预测（OCP）方法解决了这一问题，但代价是牺牲了（i）分组误差控制或（ii）与学习率无关的实现。分组条件覆盖对于不同数据点集合之间的公平性以及提供更精细的 UQ 保证至关重要。无参数优化对于对抗性和未知的数据偏移的鲁棒性至关重要。我们提出了一种用于分组条件 OCP 的无参数算法，并证明其实现了最佳的分组条件覆盖保证。我们在合成和真实世界数据上评估了我们的算法，结果表明我们的方法不仅提高了现有无参数 OCP 方法的可靠性，而且提供了与经过精心调优的分组条件方法在大小上相当的预测区间。通过将分组条件覆盖与无参数在线算法相统一，我们的工作为在偏移环境下的公平且鲁棒的不确定性量化奠定了基础。
AI.summary: 本文针对数据分布随时间偏移的在线不确定性量化问题，提出了一种无参数的分组条件在线共形预测算法。该方法克服了现有方法在分组误差控制与学习率独立实现之间不可兼得的缺陷，在合成和真实数据集上均展现出了高可靠性和与精细调优方法相当的预测区间宽度，为实现公平且鲁棒的不确定性量化提供了新途径。
AI.keywords: 在线共形预测, 不确定性量化, 分组条件覆盖, 无参数优化, 分布偏移
AI.comments: 该论文成功地将“分组条件覆盖”（保障公平性）与“无参数在线优化”（保障对未知数据偏移的鲁棒性）结合起来，解决了在线共形预测中难以兼顾二者的痛点。其创新之处在于消除了对学习率等超参数微调的依赖，同时在理论和实验上保证了更细粒度的覆盖率。局限性在于，仅从摘要中无法得知其在面临极度极端或快速变化的非平稳数据漂移时的计算开销和理论恢复速度。

title: SF-LIFE: A Large-Scale Simulated Movement Dataset for the San Francisco Bay Area
summary: We introduce SF-LIFE, a large-scale simulated movement dataset designed to accelerate research in transportation, mobility, and machine learning. The dataset contains 3,024,000,000,000 location records capturing complete, noise-free, multi-modality trajectories of 500,000 simulated agents observed at a 1Hz frequency navigating the San Francisco Bay Area network over a 70-day period. The data captures (1) needs-driven daily agendas of individual agents generated by an agent-based simulation of human patterns of life and (2) detailed kinematic trajectories moving agents across the OpenStreetMap representation of San Francisco using data from 40+ transit agencies across 9 counties. SF-LIFE provides unprecedented scale and detail as trajectories are based on real transit infrastructure using San Francisco General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) data, having agent movements across multiple modalities, including bus, rail, bike, automobile, and walking. For this high-fidelity simulated representation of San Francisco, we provide (1) the full trajectory data annotated with transportation mode labels, (2) reduced-size versions of the trajectory data with reduced temporal frequency, (3) agent activity information describing the causal activity why an agent visits a place, (4) agent demographic data, and (5) the underlying OSM road network and building data. As the first dataset of its scale and level of detail, SF-LIFE overcomes the privacy, noise, and completeness limitations inherent in real-world tracking data, providing a robust and ethically sourced resource for research in transit optimization, human mobility analysis, and urban computing.

AI.title_translation: SF-LIFE：旧金山湾区大规模模拟移动数据集
AI.tldr: 本文推出了SF-LIFE，一个包含50万模拟智能体在旧金山湾区70天内高精度（1Hz）多模态移动轨迹的超大规模模拟数据集，旨在克服真实数据在隐私、噪声和完整性方面的限制。
AI.motivation: 真实世界的轨迹跟踪数据通常受到隐私保护限制、数据噪声以及数据不完整性的制约，这阻碍了交通、人类移动性分析和机器学习等领域的研究。因此，亟需一个大规模、高保真、无噪声且合乎伦理的模拟移动数据集。
AI.method:
1. 基于智能体的人类生活模式模拟，生成个体智能体需求驱动的每日活动议程。
2. 结合来自9个县、40多个交通机构的旧金山通用公交数据规范（GTFS）数据，在OpenStreetMap（OSM）道路网络上模拟智能体的高精度运动学轨迹。
3. 以1Hz的高频率记录50万个智能体在70天内的多模态（公交、铁路、自行车、汽车、步行）移动过程。
AI.result: 成功构建并提供了SF-LIFE数据集，其中包含3.024万亿条高频位置记录。具体提供的数据包括：带有出行模式标注的完整轨迹数据、降频版轨迹数据、智能体出行因果活动信息、智能体人口统计数据，以及底层的OSM路网和建筑物数据。
AI.conclusion: SF-LIFE是首个达到如此规模和细节水平的模拟移动数据集，它成功克服了真实世界跟踪数据中固有的隐私、噪声和不完整性限制，为交通优化、人类移动性分析和城市计算研究提供了一个强大、鲁棒且符合伦理的研究资源。
AI.translation: 我们引入了SF-LIFE，这是一个大规模的模拟移动数据集，旨在加速交通、移动性和机器学习领域的研究。该数据集包含3,024,000,000,000条位置记录，捕捉了50万个模拟智能体在旧金山湾区网络中、70天内以1Hz频率导航的完整、无噪声、多模态轨迹。该数据捕捉了：（1）由人类生活模式的基于智能体模拟生成的个体智能体需求驱动的日常议程，以及（2）利用来自9个县、40多个交通机构的数据，在旧金山OpenStreetMap（OSM）表示上移动智能体的详细运动学轨迹。由于轨迹基于真实的交通基础设施并使用旧金山通用公交数据规范（GTFS）数据，SF-LIFE提供了前所未有的规模和细节，涵盖了多种出行方式（包括公交、铁路、自行车、汽车和步行）的智能体移动。针对旧金山的这一高保真模拟表示，我们提供了：（1）带有交通模式标签的完整轨迹数据，（2）具有较低时间频率的简化版轨迹数据，（3）描述智能体访问某地因果活动的智能体活动信息，（4）智能体人口统计数据，以及（5）底层的OSM道路网络和建筑物数据。作为首个具有如此规模和细节水平的数据集，SF-LIFE克服了真实世界跟踪数据中固有的隐私、噪声和完整性限制，为交通优化、人类移动性分析和城市计算研究提供了一个强大且来源符合伦理的资源。
AI.summary: 本文介绍了SF-LIFE，这是一个用于旧金山湾区的大规模高保真模拟移动数据集。该数据集包含50万个模拟智能体在70天内以1Hz频率产生的3.024万亿条多模态移动轨迹。数据集基于真实的GTFS公交数据和OSM路网，不仅包含完整的轨迹和出行模式标注，还提供了智能体活动、人口统计学及底层地理信息。SF-LIFE旨在解决真实世界轨迹数据的隐私和质量限制，为城市计算和交通优化等领域提供强有力的支持。
AI.keywords: 模拟移动数据集, 智能体模拟, 人类移动性, 城市计算, 旧金山湾区
AI.comments:
1. 创新性：该研究通过基于智能体的模拟方法，成功生成了高达3万亿条记录的超大规模轨迹数据集，有效解决了真实世界轨迹数据在隐私保护、噪声干扰和数据缺失方面的瓶颈。
2. 重要性：数据集紧密结合了真实的GTFS公交数据和OSM路网，具备极高的空间和时间保真度（1Hz），为城市计算、交通系统优化和大规模机器学习模型训练提供了宝贵的基准平台。
3. 局限性：尽管保真度极高，但模拟数据在反映人类复杂、非理性或应急状态下的出行决策时，可能仍与真实世界存在一定偏差，其泛化能力需在实际应用中进一步验证。

title: Solving 2D Black Scholes Equation via Hermitian Block Embedding and Generalised Quantum Signal Processing
summary: The Black Scholes equation provides a fundamental model for the no arbitrage pricing of financial derivatives. After finite difference discretisation, the pricing problem can be formulated as a finite dimensional linear algebra problem involving the inverse of a non Hermitian time step matrix. Recent advances in quantum linear algebra algorithms, particularly the generalised quantum signal processing (GQSP)algorithm, enable matrix functions to be implemented through polynomial transformations of a suitable unitary or Hermitian form. In this paper, we develop a Hermitian block embedding method that enables GQSP to be applied to the two dimensional Black Scholes equation. Numerical simulations for two asset European call options are performed to evaluate the proposed approach. GQSP based solutions are benchmarked against the classical polynomial approximation with backward Euler finite difference method, showing close agreement. This indicates that the Hermitian block embedding construction accurately captures the dynamics of the original non Hermitian operator. These results demonstrate the feasibility of combining Hermitian block embeddings with GQSP for multidimensional Black Scholes problems and provide a proof of principle for applying modern quantum linear algebra techniques to option pricing.

AI.title_translation: 基于厄米分块嵌入和广义量子信号处理求解二维Black-Scholes方程
AI.tldr: 本文开发了一种厄米分块嵌入方法，成功将广义量子信号处理（GQSP）应用于二维Black-Scholes方程，并通过双资产期权模拟验证了其与传统经典方法的高度一致性。
AI.motivation: 在有限差分离散化后，Black-Scholes期权定价问题会转化为涉及非厄米时间步长矩阵求逆的线性代数问题。虽然近年来的广义量子信号处理（GQSP）等算法允许通过多项式变换实现矩阵函数，但它们需要幺正或厄米形式。因此，需要一种方法将非厄米算子转化为适用于GQSP的格式。
AI.method: 开发了一种厄米分块嵌入方法，使广义量子信号处理（GQSP）算法能够应用于二维Black-Scholes方程，并通过双资产欧式看涨期权的数值模拟对该方法进行了评估。
AI.result: 基于GQSP的求解方案与传统的后向欧拉有限差分多项式逼近方法进行了基准对比，结果显示出高度一致。这表明所提出的厄米分块嵌入构建能够准确捕捉原始非厄米算子的动力学特征。
AI.conclusion: 数值模拟结果证明了将厄米分块嵌入与GQSP相结合解决多维Black-Scholes问题的可行性，为将现代量子线性代数技术应用于期权定价提供了一项原理性证明。
AI.translation: Black-Scholes方程为金融衍生品的无套利定价提供了一个基本模型。在有限差分离散化之后，定价问题可以表述为一个涉及非厄米时间步长矩阵求逆的有限维线性代数问题。量子线性代数算法的最新进展，特别是广义量子信号处理（GQSP）算法，使得矩阵函数能够通过合适的幺正或厄米形式的多项式变换来实现。在本文中，我们开发了一种厄米分块嵌入方法，使GQSP能够应用于二维Black-Scholes方程。我们对双资产欧式看涨期权进行了数值模拟，以评估所提出的方法。将基于GQSP的解决方案与传统的后向欧拉有限差分多项式逼近方法进行了基准对比，结果显示出高度一致。这表明厄米分块嵌入构建准确地捕捉了原始非厄米算子的动力学特征。这些结果证明了将厄米分块嵌入与GQSP相结合来解决多维Black-Scholes问题的可行性，并为将现代量子线性代数技术应用于期权定价提供了原理性证明。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种结合厄米分块嵌入与广义量子信号处理（GQSP）的新方法，用于求解二维Black-Scholes方程。通过将非厄米时间步长矩阵嵌入到厄米矩阵中，使GQSP能够应用于期权定价问题。双资产欧式看涨期权的数值模拟表明，该方法与传统经典算法高度吻合，验证了其可行性。
AI.keywords: Black-Scholes方程, 广义量子信号处理 (GQSP), 厄米分块嵌入, 期权定价, 量子线性代数
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于首次将厄米分块嵌入方法与广义量子信号处理（GQSP）相结合，解决了二维Black-Scholes方程离散化后矩阵非厄米性带来的量子求解难题。其重要性在于为现代量子线性代数算法在金融衍生品定价领域的实际应用提供了可行性证明（Proof of Principle）。局限性在于目前仅在二维双资产欧式看涨期权上进行了数值模拟验证，对于更高维度以及在实际量子硬件上的运行表现还有待进一步研究。

title: Continuous Data Assimilation with Learned Surrogate Dynamics
summary: Continuous data assimilation seeks to estimate the state of a dynamical system from partial observations. In many applications, however, the state dynamics are unknown or prohibitively expensive to simulate at the required resolution, leading to model error. Motivated by this challenge and the increasing adoption of machine learning surrogates in data assimilation, this paper develops a unified finite-dimensional analysis of nudging algorithms that employ learned surrogate models of the dynamics. We first establish general conditions on the dynamics and observations that guarantee accurate tracking for nudging with the true dynamics model, both in the noise-free and noisy settings. We then show that nudging algorithms that employ surrogate models retain exponential convergence up to an explicit error floor that quantifies the effects of surrogate approximation error and observation noise. Finally, we analyze surrogate models obtained by learning either the vector field or the short-time solution map of the system, and quantify the amount of training data needed to ensure accurate nudging in the noise-free setting. Numerical experiments support the theory.

AI.title_translation: 基于学习代理动力学的连续数据同化
AI.tldr: 本文对使用机器学习代理动力学模型的nudging数据同化算法进行了统一的有限维分析，证明了其具有指数收敛性，并量化了误差下限及所需的训练数据量。
AI.motivation: 在连续数据同化中，动力系统的状态动力学往往未知，或者在高分辨率下进行模拟的计算成本过于昂贵，从而导致模型误差。为了解决这一挑战，并响应在数据同化中越来越多采用机器学习代理模型的趋势，需要对这些结合了代理模型的算法进行理论分析。
AI.method: 本文开发了一种统一的有限维分析方法，用于研究采用学习到的动力学代理模型的nudging算法。具体分析了通过学习系统的向量场（vector field）或短时解映射（short-time solution map）构建的代理模型，并量化了在无噪声环境下确保准确跟踪所需的训练数据量。
AI.result: 1. 确立了在无噪声和有噪声设置下，使用真实动力学模型进行nudging时保证准确跟踪的一般条件；2. 证明了采用代理模型的nudging算法能够保持指数收敛性，直至一个量化了代理逼近误差和观测噪声影响的显式误差下限；3. 量化了在无噪声设置下确保准确nudging所需的训练数据量。数值实验验证了这些理论结果。
AI.conclusion: 使用学习得到的代理动力学模型的nudging算法在数据同化中是可行且有效的。该算法不仅保留了指数收敛性，而且其误差界和所需的训练数据量可以通过理论进行显式量化。
AI.translation: 连续数据同化旨在通过部分观测来估计动力系统的状态。然而，在许多应用中，状态动力学是未知的，或者在所需分辨率下进行模拟的成本高得令人望而却步，从而导致模型误差。受这一挑战以及机器学习代理模型在数据同化中日益广泛应用的启发，本文对采用学习到的动力学代理模型的nudging算法进行了统一的有限维分析。我们首先确立了在无噪声和有噪声设置下，使用真实动力学模型进行nudging时保证准确跟踪的动力学和观测的一般条件。然后，我们表明采用代理模型的nudging算法保留了指数收敛性，直至一个量化了代理逼近误差和观测噪声影响的显式误差下限。最后，我们分析了通过学习系统的向量场或短时解映射获得的代理模型，并量化了在无噪声设置下确保准确nudging所需的训练数据量。数值实验支持了该理论。
AI.summary: 本文针对动力系统动力学未知或模拟成本高昂的问题，研究了结合机器学习代理动力学模型的连续数据同化（nudging算法）。作者提出了一个统一的有限维分析框架，证明了该方法在存在代理逼近误差和观测噪声的情况下仍能保持指数收敛性，并给出了显式的误差下限。此外，文章还量化了学习向量场或短时解映射所需的训练数据量，并通过数值实验验证了理论的正确性。
AI.keywords: 连续数据同化, 代理动力学, Nudging算法, 机器学习, 收敛性分析
AI.comments: 本文的创新之处在于为结合机器学习代理模型的nudging数据同化算法提供了坚实的理论基础（有限维分析），不仅证明了指数收敛性，还给出了显式的误差界和样本复杂度（训练数据量）量化。这对于桥接传统数据同化与现代机器学习方法具有重要意义。局限性在于该分析可能主要局限于有限维系统，且对实际复杂高维物理系统的泛化能力仍有待在更广泛的场景中验证。

title: Annotation-Informed Block-Sparse Bayesian Modeling for cis-Expression Prediction
summary: Genotype-based cis-expression prediction depends on accurately modeling local regulatory architecture. We present block-sparse Bayesian sparse linear mixed model (bsBSLMM), an extension of Bayesian sparse linear mixed model (BSLMM) that incorporates linkage disequilibrium (LD)-block spike-and-slab sparsity and a transcription start site (TSS)-informed SNP inclusion prior. Across 23,098 genes from GEUVADIS European-ancestry lymphoblastoid cell lines, bsBSLMM retained more predictable genes than BSLMM, LASSO, BLUP, TIGAR elastic net, and TIGAR Dirichlet-process regression under matched evaluation criteria. Compared with BSLMM, bsBSLMM improved held-out prediction performance for most shared genes, with gains driven primarily by LD-block sparsity and further enhanced by the TSS-informed prior. Variants selected by bsBSLMM showed stronger enrichment in GM12878 DNase and H3K27ac regulatory regions than variants selected by BSLMM. In transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) analysis, bsBSLMM recovered established inflammatory bowel disease signals, including IL23R, and identified additional genome-wide significant genes not detected by BSLMM. Independent validation in the Louisiana Osteoporosis Study reproduced the increased prediction yield across ancestries and recovered biologically relevant bone mineral density pathways in downstream TWAS and gene set enrichment analyses. These results demonstrate that incorporating LD-block structure and biologically informed SNP priors improves cis-expression prediction and enhances downstream TWAS discovery.

AI.title_translation: 基于注释指导的分块稀疏贝叶斯模型用于顺式表达预测
AI.tldr: 本文提出了bsBSLMM模型，通过在贝叶斯框架中引入LD分块稀疏性和TSS生物学注释先验，显著提升了顺式表达预测的准确性及下游TWAS的发现效能。
AI.motivation: 基于基因型的顺式表达预测依赖于对局部调控架构的精确建模。现有的预测模型未能充分利用连锁不平衡（LD）分块结构和生物学功能注释（如TSS），从而限制了预测的准确性和下游关联分析的效能。
AI.method: 提出分块稀疏贝叶斯稀疏线性混合模型（bsBSLMM）。该模型是贝叶斯稀疏线性混合模型（BSLMM）的扩展，它融合了连锁不平衡（LD）分块的“spike-and-slab”稀疏性以及由转录起始位点（TSS）指导的SNP引入先验。
AI.result: 在GEUVADIS数据集的23,098个基因中，bsBSLMM保留的可预测基因多于BSLMM、LASSO、BLUP、TIGAR弹性网络和TIGAR狄利克雷过程回归。相比于BSLMM，bsBSLMM提升了多数共享基因的留出预测性能，且选择的变异在GM12878 DNase和H3K27ac调控区域表现出更强的富集。在TWAS分析中，bsBSLMM成功恢复了已知的炎症性肠病信号（包括IL23R），并检测到了BSLMM未发现的显著基因。这些结果在路易斯安那骨质疏松症研究中得到了独立验证。
AI.conclusion: 结合连锁不平衡（LD）分块结构和生物学知情的SNP先验，能够有效改善顺式表达预测的准确性，并显著增强下游全转录组关联分析（TWAS）的基因发现能力。
AI.translation: 基于基因型的顺式表达预测依赖于对局部调控架构的精确建模。我们提出了分块稀疏贝叶斯稀疏线性混合模型（bsBSLMM），它是贝叶斯稀疏线性混合模型（BSLMM）的扩展，融合了连锁不平衡（LD）分块的“spike-and-slab”稀疏性以及受转录起始位点（TSS）启发的SNP引入先验。在来自GEUVADIS欧洲血统淋巴母细胞系的23,098个基因中，在匹配的评估标准下，bsBSLMM比BSLMM、LASSO、BLUP、TIGAR弹性网络和TIGAR狄利克雷过程回归保留了更多可预测的基因。与BSLMM相比，bsBSLMM提高了大多数共享基因的留出预测性能，这些提升主要由LD分块稀疏性驱动，并由TSS先验进一步增强。与BSLMM选择的变异相比，bsBSLMM选择的变异在GM12878 DNase和H3K27ac调控区域表现出更强的富集。在全转录组关联研究（TWAS）分析中，bsBSLMM恢复了已建立的炎症性肠病信号（包括IL23R），并识别出了BSLMM未检测到的其他全基因组显著基因。在路易斯安那骨质疏松症研究中的独立验证重现了跨祖先预测产量的增加，并在下游TWAS和基因集富集分析中恢复了生物学相关的骨密度通路。这些结果表明，结合LD分块结构和生物学知情的SNP先验可以改善顺式表达预测，并增强下游TWAS的发现。
AI.summary: 本文提出了一种名为bsBSLMM的贝叶斯线性混合模型扩展方法，该方法通过引入连锁不平衡（LD）分块稀疏性和转录起始位点（TSS）先验来优化顺式基因表达预测。实验表明，bsBSLMM在基因表达预测准确性、调控区域富集度以及下游转录组关联分析（TWAS）的基因发现能力上均显著优于现有主流方法，并具有跨祖先的独立验证可靠性。
AI.keywords: 顺式表达预测, 贝叶斯稀疏线性混合模型, 连锁不平衡分块, 转录起始位点, 转录组关联分析
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地将生物学先验（TSS和连锁不平衡LD分块）融入到统计遗传学预测模型中，有效解决了传统方法忽略局部染色质结构和调控特异性的局限。这对于提高TWAS的功效和解释性具有重要意义，展示了将生物学注释与统计建模相结合的巨大潜力。

title: Joint Optimization of Qubit Leasing and Quantum Circuit Distribution
summary: We consider an agent, who would like to execute a given quantum circuit using resources leased from a set of quantum computers (QCs) connected by a quantum network. For this purpose, the agent needs to make the following four key decisions: (i) how many qubits to lease from each QC, (ii) at which QCs to store different circuit qubits in different time slots, (iii) at which QC to execute each gate in the circuit, and (iv) how to move qubits between QCs, choosing between migration and teleportation. We refer to this problem facing the agent as the joint qubit leasing and quantum circuit distribution (JQLQCD) problem, and provide a comprehensive integer linear programming (ILP) formulation for it. We show that the JQLQCD problem is NP-complete. Next, we identify several special cases in which the problem can be optimally solved in closed form or via polynomial-time algorithms. Also, we propose a greedy algorithm with local search refinement to solve large instances of the general JQLQCD problem. Finally, we evaluate the performance of the proposed greedy algorithm using extensive numerical computations.

AI.title_translation: 量子比特租赁与量子电路分布的联合优化
AI.tldr: 本文研究了分布式量子计算中的量子比特租赁与电路分布联合优化问题（JQLQCD），提出了整数线性规划模型，并设计了一种高效的带局部搜索的贪婪算法。
AI.motivation: 在由量子网络连接的多个量子计算机（QC）环境中，用户需要租用资源来执行量子电路。为了最小化成本或优化效率，用户必须联合决策量子比特租赁数量、存储位置、门操作执行位置以及量子比特在QC之间的传输方式。
AI.method: 1. 将联合量子比特租赁与量子电路分布（JQLQCD）问题建模为一个全面的整数线性规划（ILP）公式；2. 证明了该问题的NP完全性；3. 识别出若干可在多项式时间内或以闭式解形式最优求解的特殊情况；4. 提出了一种结合局部搜索细化策略的贪婪算法，用于解决大规模的通用JQLQCD问题。
AI.result: 构建了JQLQCD问题的完整ILP数学模型，并证明其为NP完全问题；识别了可快速求解的特殊场景；数值计算结果表明，所提出的带有局部搜索的贪婪算法在解决大规模问题实例时具有良好的性能。
AI.conclusion: 本文成功为JQLQCD问题建立了系统性的数学模型，并提供了从精确求解到近似启发式求解的完整算法方案，为分布式量子计算中的资源管理提供了理论和实践指导。
AI.translation: 我们考虑一个代理，该代理希望利用从通过量子网络连接的一组量子计算机（QC）中租赁的资源来执行给定的量子电路。为此，该代理需要做出以下四个关键决策：（i）从每个QC租赁多少个量子比特，（ii）在不同的时间段将不同的电路量子比特存储在哪些QC中，（iii）在哪个QC中执行电路中的每个门，以及（iv）如何在QC之间移动量子比特（在迁移和隐形传态之间进行选择）。我们将代理面临的这个问题称为联合量子比特租赁与量子电路分布（JQLQCD）问题，并为此提出了一个全面的整数线性规划（ILP）公式。我们证明了JQLQCD问题是NP完全的。接着，我们确定了几种特殊情况，在这些情况下，该问题可以通过闭式或多项式时间算法得到最优解。此外，我们提出了一种带有局部搜索细化的贪婪算法，以解决通用JQLQCD问题的大规模实例。最后，我们通过广泛的数值计算评估了所提贪婪算法的性能。
AI.summary: 本文研究了在网络化量子计算机环境中，如何联合优化量子比特租赁与量子电路分布（JQLQCD）的问题。作者提出了整数线性规划（ILP）模型，证明了该问题的NP完全性，并针对大规模计算场景设计了带局部搜索的贪婪算法，最后通过数值模拟验证了算法的有效性。
AI.keywords: 量子计算, 资源租赁, 电路分布, 整数线性规划, 贪婪算法
AI.comments: 该论文的创新点在于将量子比特租赁决策与量子电路的分布式执行相结合，综合考虑了量子比特的存储、门操作执行以及传输方式（迁移或隐形传态）的选择。其局限性可能在于，所提出的贪婪算法在极端复杂的异构量子网络环境中的理论近似比尚未给出，且实际量子网络中的噪声和退相干效应对优化的影响有待进一步探讨。

title: In-Expectation Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods under Heavy-Tailed Noise
summary: Many stochastic gradient methods are believed not to converge when the noise in stochastic gradients has only a finite $p$-th moment for $p\in\left(1,2\right)$, a setting known as the heavy-tailed noise assumption. However, some recent studies have found that Stochastic Gradient Descent ($\textsf{SGD}$), without any modification to its update rule, can surprisingly converge in expectation for convex problems with bounded domains, highlighting the potential of classical stochastic gradient methods. Inspired by this recent progress, we provide a comprehensive study of stochastic optimization under heavy-tailed noise and establish new in-expectation convergence results for Stochastic Mirror Descent ($\textsf{SMD}$) and Accelerated Stochastic Mirror Descent ($\textsf{ASMD}$) in convex optimization, and for $\textsf{SGD}$ and Stochastic Gradient Descent with Momentum ($\textsf{SGDM}$) in nonconvex optimization. Notably, our results not only hold without algorithmic changes but also avoid restrictive assumptions, such as bounded domains, imposed in prior work. More importantly, our analysis provides a new, elegant, and powerful framework for studying heavy-tailed stochastic optimization, opening a new route to understanding first-order stochastic gradient methods.

AI.title_translation: 重尾噪声下随机梯度方法的期望收敛性
AI.tldr: 本文证明了经典随机梯度方法（如SMD、ASMD、SGD和SGDM）在重尾噪声下无需修改算法或施加有界定义域等苛刻假设即可实现期望收敛，并为此提供了一个全新的分析框架。
AI.motivation: 在随机梯度噪声仅具有有限 $p$ 阶矩（$p \in (1,2)$，即重尾噪声）的设定下，许多随机梯度方法被认为无法收敛。尽管最近的研究发现经典的SGD在有界定义域的凸问题中可以期望收敛，但这些研究仍受限于有界定义域等严格假设。因此，本文旨在对重尾噪声下的随机优化进行全面研究，消除这些限制性假设并拓展到更多算法和非凸场景。
AI.method: 本文提供了一个全新、简洁且强大的分析框架，用于研究重尾随机优化。在此框架下，作者在不改变算法更新规则且不引入有界定义域等苛刻假设的前提下，对凸优化中的随机镜像下降（SMD）和加速随机镜像下降（ASMD），以及非凸优化中的随机梯度下降（SGD）和带动量的随机梯度下降（SGDM）进行了收敛性分析。
AI.result: 成功建立了SMD和ASMD在凸优化中、以及SGD和SGDM在非凸优化中的全新期望收敛性结果。这些结果不仅在不进行算法修改的情况下成立，而且成功避免了以往研究中必须引入的有界定义域等限制性假设。
AI.conclusion: 经典的随机梯度方法在重尾噪声下具有强大的收敛潜力，无需修改算法或施加严格的有界定义域假设即可实现期望收敛。所提出的分析框架为理解一阶随机梯度方法开辟了新途径。
AI.translation: 许多人认为，当随机梯度中的噪声仅具有有限的 $p$ 阶矩（其中 $p\in\left(1,2\right)$，这一设定被称为重尾噪声假设）时，许多随机梯度方法是无法收敛的。然而，最近的一些研究发现，随机梯度下降（SGD）在不对其更新规则进行任何修改的情况下，令人惊讶地可以在有界定义域的凸问题中实现期望收敛，这突显了经典随机梯度方法的潜力。受此最新进展的启发，我们对重尾噪声下的随机优化进行了全面研究，并为凸优化中的随机镜像下降（SMD）和加速随机镜像下降（ASMD），以及非凸优化中的随机梯度下降（SGD）和带动量的随机梯度下降（SGDM）建立了新的期望收敛结果。值得注意的是，我们的结果不仅在不改变算法的情况下成立，而且避免了先前工作中施加的限制性假设（例如有界定义域）。更重要的是，我们的分析为研究重尾随机优化提供了一个全新、优雅且强大的框架，为理解一阶随机梯度方法开辟了一条新途径。
AI.summary: 本文针对重尾噪声（即噪声仅具有有限的 $p$ 阶矩， $p\in(1,2)$）下的随机优化问题展开了系统研究。作者在不修改算法且不依赖“有界定义域”等限制性假设的前提下，证明了凸优化中的SMD和ASMD、以及非凸优化中的SGD和SGDM的期望收敛性。该研究不仅拓宽了经典一阶随机梯度方法的理论边界，还提供了一个用于分析重尾随机优化的全新理论框架。
AI.keywords: 重尾噪声, 期望收敛性, 随机梯度下降, 随机镜像下降, 凸与非凸优化
AI.comments: 本文的重要创新在于打破了以往关于重尾噪声下随机梯度方法必须进行算法修改（如梯度裁剪）或限制在有界定义域内才能收敛的传统认知。通过提出一种全新且通用的分析框架，本文成功证明了多种经典算法（SMD、ASMD、SGD、SGDM）在凸和非凸设定下的期望收敛性。这一成果具有极高的理论价值，为理解一阶随机梯度方法在恶劣噪声环境下的表现开辟了新的理论途径。

title: Spectra-Guided Neural Tucker Factorization
summary: This paper proposes Spectra-Guided Neural Tucker Factorization (SG-NTF) for High-Dimensional and Incomplete (HDI) tensor completion. Circumventing discrete representational limits, SG-NTF maps scalar timestamps into a continuous spectral space to abstract temporal periodicities. Concurrently, a Spatio-Temporal Co-Gating (STCG) mechanism explicitly filters latent interactions via multiplicative modulation on spatiotemporal contexts. Evaluations on real-world HDI tensors verify that SG-NTF maintains competitive completion accuracy with parameter efficiency.

AI.tldr: 提出SG-NTF方法，通过将时间戳映射到连续谱空间并结合时空协门控机制，实现了高效且精准的高维不完整张量补全。
AI.motivation: 旨在解决高维不完整（HDI）张量补全中，由于离散表示的限制而难以有效建模和捕捉时间周期性的问题。
AI.method: 提出谱引导的神经Tucker分解（SG-NTF）方法。该方法将标量时间戳映射到连续谱空间以抽象时间周期性，并引入时空协门控（STCG）机制，通过对时空上下文进行乘性调制来显式过滤潜在的交互作用。
AI.result: 在真实世界HDI张量上的评估结果表明，SG-NTF在保持参数高效性的同时，能够实现具有竞争力的补全准确率。
AI.conclusion: SG-NTF为高维不完整张量补全提供了一种兼顾高参数效率与高预测精度的有效解决方案。
AI.translation: 本文提出了一种用于高维不完整（HDI）张量补全的谱引导神经Tucker分解（SG-NTF）方法。为了规避离散表示的局限性，SG-NTF将标量时间戳映射到连续的谱空间中，以抽象出时间周期性。同时，时空协门控（STCG）机制通过对时空上下文进行乘性调制，显式地过滤潜在的交互作用。在真实世界HDI张量上的评估证实，SG-NTF在保持参数效率的同时，具有竞争力的补全准确度。
AI.summary: 本文针对高维不完整（HDI）张量补全问题，提出了一种名为SG-NTF的新方法。该方法通过将时间戳映射到连续谱空间来克服离散表示的局限，从而更好地捕捉时间周期性，并结合时空协门控（STCG）机制来优化时空特征的交互。实验表明，该方法在保证参数效率的前提下实现了高精度的张量补全。
AI.keywords: 张量补全, Tucker分解, 连续谱空间, 时空建模
AI.comments: 该研究巧妙地将连续谱映射与门控机制相结合，有效解决了高维张量补全中传统离散时间表示难以捕捉周期性特征的局限性。方法在维持较低参数量的同时保证了高补全精度，具有良好的实用价值。然而，摘要中未提及该方法在面对非周期性时序波动时的鲁棒性，以及在大规模数据集上的计算复杂度表现。

title: Hashprice modulates the electricity demand response of Bitcoin miners
comments: This manuscript has supplementary information in the accompanying PDF
summary: Large, fast-controllable loads such as Bitcoin mining facilities are increasingly viewed as potential sources of flexibility in modern power systems, yet the conditions under which this flexibility is realized remain incompletely understood. Using the Texas power market as an empirical setting, we examine how Bitcoin-mining load responds to two distinct electricity-sector cost channels: contemporaneous wholesale electricity prices and incentives created by coincident-peak-based transmission charges. We find that mining load responds to both cost channels in a manner consistent with miners operating around a breakeven point. At the aggregate level, we observe that mining load decreases as electricity-sector costs rise, but the strength of this response depends on hashprice, a measure of expected mining revenue from the crypto-financial sector. When hashprice is higher, aggregate load responsiveness is weaker. This mechanism is especially evident in the wholesale-price response. Mining load remains largely online at low prices and begins to decline only when electricity costs become large relative to expected mining revenue, with higher hashprice shifting the implied curtailment threshold toward higher wholesale prices. These findings indicate that Bitcoin-mining demand response to electricity-sector costs is economically state-dependent and shaped by revenue conditions in the crypto-financial sector. Treating such loads as stable demand-response resources may therefore overstate available grid flexibility, with implications for power-system planning, market design, and reliability assessment.
